Fix an integer $\ell\ge3$ and set $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, so the multiplicative order of $q^2$ is $\ell$. Use the divided-power integral form of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] from [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], specialized by $v\mapsto q$ to $\mathbb C$. In type $A_1$, write $K=K_h$ and $E,F$ for the rank-one generators. The convention is

$$KEK^{-1}=q^2E,\qquad KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}F,\qquad [E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}},$$

$$\Delta(K)=K\otimes K,\qquad \Delta(E)=E\otimes K+1\otimes E,\qquad \Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes F.$$

This is the Sawin coproduct, rather than the inverse-$K$ coproduct in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Its counit is $\varepsilon(K)=1$, $\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon(F)=0$ and its antipode is $S(E)=-EK^{-1}$, $S(F)=-KF$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$. The exact integral transport is from the library algebra with opposite coproduct, by $E_{\rm target}=KE_{\rm lib}$, $F_{\rm target}=F_{\rm lib}K^{-1}$ and $K_{\rm target}=K_{\rm lib}$. Substituting these generators gives the displayed coproduct and unchanged mixed relation. On divided powers the formulas are $E_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{-r(r-1)}K^rE_{\rm lib}^{(r)}$ and $F_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{r(r-1)}F_{\rm lib}^{(r)}K^{-r}$; the inverse formulas also have Laurent-monomial coefficients, so the integral lattice and toral generators are preserved.

The Lusztig specialization includes all divided powers $E^{(r)},F^{(r)}$ and the toral quantum binomials; this is the divided-power form, not the small quantum group. A finite-dimensional module is **type 1** when it carries its integral-weight grading $M=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}M_m$ with $K|_{M_m}=q^m$, the full toral character $T_{c,t}|_{M_m}=\begin{bmatrix}m+c\\t\end{bmatrix}_q I$ for every $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$, and $E^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m+2r}$, $F^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m-2r}$. The binomial is its Laurent-polynomial specialization, including negative upper indices. The grading is part of the data and is not collapsed when distinct weights have the same $K$ eigenvalue. Every module intertwiner preserves it: for $m<n$, $T_{-m,n-m}$ has eigenvalues $0$ and $1$ on weights $m$ and $n$.

For $a\ge0$, the Weyl module $\Delta(a)$ has basis $v_0,\ldots,v_a$ and actions

$$Kv_j=q^{a-2j}v_j,\qquad E^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}a-j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j-r},\qquad F^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j+r},$$

where the Gaussian binomials are the Laurent-polynomial specializations of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], and $v_j=0$ outside $0\le j\le a$. Its dual is the dual Weyl module $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. A **Weyl filtration** (respectively dual-Weyl filtration) is a finite submodule filtration whose successive quotients are modules $\Delta(a)$ (respectively $\nabla(a)$). A **tilting module** is a module with both filtrations.

Take $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, so $s^2=q$. The ribbon category is the full weight-lattice extension $\mathcal U_s^\dagger(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ of this Lusztig form, not its root-lattice restriction. Its toral factor is the completed function algebra on the weight lattice $P=\mathbb Z\omega$, acting on each weight space by its weight character. Before specialization, the rank-one universal $R$-matrix is the Sawin weight-lattice expression

$R=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E^{(r)}\otimes F^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$

interpreted in the completed tensor product; at the root it means the image of the integral completed form, not termwise division by a vanishing $[r]_q!$. In ordinary powers the coefficient is $q^{r(r-1)/2}(q-q^{-1})^r/[r]_q!$; changing to two divided powers multiplies that coefficient by $([r]_q!)^2$. Thus the displayed divided-power coefficient is Laurent integral and vanishes for $r\ge\ell$ after specialization. The toral factor is the weight pairing, fixed explicitly by $D$ above. The pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and the twist is $\theta=u^{-1}j$ for the Drinfeld map $u$. The object class of this page is the full subcategory of finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting modules for this weight-lattice ribbon extension. No assertion about semisimplicity or the trace radical is part of this definition.

Use the full integral-weight divided-power category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], with $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$ and every $\ell\ge3$. The displayed strings define $\Delta(a)$, and $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. For all $a,b\ge0$,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=\delta_{ab},\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=0.$$

Here Ext vanishing means that every short exact sequence in the finite-dimensional full-weight category with those end terms splits. The tensor product $\Delta(a)\otimes\Delta(b)$ has one Weyl factor of each label $a+b,a+b-2,\ldots,|a-b|$, and the analogous dual-Weyl assertion holds. Both filtration classes are closed under direct summands. Thus tiltings are closed under tensor products, duals and direct summands. For every $a\ge0$ there is exactly one indecomposable tilting $T(a)$ of highest weight $a$; its weight-$a$ space is one-dimensional, and it occurs as a summand of $V^{\otimes a}$, where $V=\Delta(1)$. Every finite tilting is a finite direct sum of these $T(a)$, so the additive idempotent-complete tensor category generated by $V$ is the entire tilting category.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and use the full-weight category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Write $T(m)$ for the indecomposable tilting of highest weight $m$ and $\chi(m)=\sum_{j=0}^m e^{m-2j}$. For $a\ge1$ and $0\le b\le\ell-2$,

$$\operatorname{ch}T(a\ell+b)=\chi(a\ell+b)+\chi(a\ell-b-2),\qquad \operatorname{ch}T(a\ell-1)=\chi(a\ell-1).$$

Also $T(m)=\Delta(m)=\nabla(m)$ for $0\le m<\ell$. With the positive $K$ pivotal map, the dimension on a Weyl character is $[m+1]_q$. Consequently every $T(m)$ with $m\ge\ell-1$ has zero pivotal trace on **every** endomorphism, so its identity is negligible. In the retained range $0\le m\le\ell-2$, $T(m)$ is simple of nonzero pivotal dimension $[m+1]_q$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be an additive $\mathbb C$-linear rigid monoidal category with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=\mathbb C$, and fix a pivotal structure $j_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ as in [[def-pivotal-structure]]. For $f:X\to Y$, call $f$ **negligible** if

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X\circ g\circ f)=0\qquad\text{for every }g:Y\to X,$$

where the left trace is [[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]. The negligible morphisms form the intersection of the kernels of these linear functionals; this definition alone does not assert tensor-ideal closure.

For the complex Temperley–Lieb diagram category, use its cup/cap pivotal structure. The resulting trace is exactly the unnormalized planar closure of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]]. The same definition applies to the complex type-1 tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]] when its stated ribbon pivotal structure is used.

In the pivotal setting of [[def-negligible-morphism-in-a-pivotal-category]], the negligible morphisms are closed under addition, scalar multiplication, arbitrary composition on either side, and tensor product on either side. Thus they form a two-sided tensor ideal. The proof uses an explicit partial-trace identity and does not assume that an arbitrary intertwiner of a tensor product factors as a tensor product of intertwiners.

For every $\ell\ge3$, the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]] is rigid and braided by $c_{M,N}=\operatorname{flip}\circ R_{M,N}$, where

$$R_{M,N}=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E_M^{(r)}\otimes F_N^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$$

The sum is finite on every pair of objects. Its pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and its ribbon twist is $\theta_M=u_M^{-1}j_M$, with $u$ the Drinfeld map. For $V=\Delta(1)$, the self-dual cup and cap are

$$w=v_+\otimes v_- -q^{-1}v_-\otimes v_+,\qquad b(v_+\otimes v_-)=-q,\quad b(v_-\otimes v_+)=1,$$

with $b(v_\pm\otimes v_\pm)=0$. They obey both snakes, $b(w)=-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$ for $j$. Nevertheless $\dim_j V=\delta$. If $U=-wb$, then $U^2=\delta U$, the adjacent TL relations hold, and

$$c_{V,V}=sI-s^{-1}U,\qquad T=qU-I=-s\,c_{V,V}^{-1}.$$

The $\Delta(2)$ and trivial channels have crossing eigenvalues $s,-s^{-3}$ and Hecke eigenvalues $-1,q^2$, respectively. Their twists are $s^8,1$; $\theta_V=s^3I$. The $\Delta(2)$ channel is removed in the negligible quotient when $\ell=3$. More generally $\theta_{\Delta(a)}=s^{a(a+2)}I$ for $0\le a\le\ell-1$. These assertions include even $\ell$ and use no small-quantum-group substitution.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

derivations.claim: By [F1] every object decomposes into finitely many indecomposable $T(m)$. By [F2], all $T(m)$ with $m\ge\ell-1$ have negligible identities and become zero. For retained $a$, $T(a)=\Delta(a)=\nabla(a)$ is simple; Hom orthogonality in [F1] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(T(a),T(b))=\delta_{ab}\mathbb C$. Thus the subcategory of retained sums has rectangular matrix Hom spaces. Its trace on each endomorphism block is $[a+1]$ times the ordinary matrix trace, by [F2,F5]. These nonzero weights make the pairing with the reverse Hom space nondegenerate. Consequently a morphism is negligible exactly when its retained-to-retained block vanishes; all its other blocks factor through negligible summands and are negligible by [F3]. Hence the quotient is precisely the semisimple category of retained sums, with the asserted complete simple list.

The tensor product and composition descend by the tensor-ideal property [F3]. The unit $T(0)$ has scalar endomorphisms and dimension $1$, so is simple and survives. The dual of $T(m)$ is an indecomposable tilting of the same highest weight: its character is symmetric, duality preserves indecomposability, and [F1] classifies it as $T(m)$. Thus duality preserves both the retained and negligible parts of step 1.1; it descends, and the evaluation/coevaluation snakes remain identities in the quotient. The invertible braidings, pivotal maps and dual-compatible twist of [F4] descend by naturality and [F3]. The quotient is therefore rigid and ribbon. Left and right pivotal traces on retained simples are respectively the sums of their $K$ and $K^{-1}$ weight eigenvalues; symmetric strings make them equal to $[a+1]$. Additivity and the matrix-block description prove equality on all endomorphisms, so the quotient is spherical.

Put $k=\ell-2$, $S_a=[T(a)]$ for $0\le a\le k$, and $x=S_1$. The tensor filtration [F1] for $V\otimes\Delta(a)$ has factors $\Delta(a+1),\Delta(a-1)$, omitting the negative label at $a=0$. For $a\le k$ these factors are simple tiltings, including $\Delta(\ell-1)$ at the boundary, by [F2]. Their extensions split by [F1]'s Ext orthogonality, since each is both Weyl and dual Weyl. Hence in the quotient $xS_a=S_{a-1}+S_{a+1}$ with $S_{-1}=S_{k+1}=0$, $S_0=1$. For $k=1$ this says $x^2=1$. Define integer polynomials $P_0=1$, $P_1=x$, $P_{a+1}=xP_a-P_{a-1}$. Then $S_a=P_a(x)$ and $P_{k+1}(x)=0$.

Induction with this recurrence gives the polynomial identity $P_aP_b=\sum_{c=|a-b|,\ |a-b|+2,\ldots,a+b}P_c$: for $b=0$ it is immediate, and subtracting the preceding $b-1$ identity from $x$ times the $b$ identity cancels its two interior shifted sums and leaves the $b+1$ endpoints. Modulo $P_{k+1}=0$, the same recurrence gives $P_{k+1+j}=-P_{k+1-j}$. The terms above $k$ in the product sum therefore cancel the retained terms from $2k+2-a-b$ upwards, with matching parity; a possible term $P_{k+1}$ is zero. The remaining indices are precisely $|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2k-a-b)$ of parity $a+b$. The simple classes are independent by step 1.1, so this class identity is the actual direct-sum multiplicity rule, not merely a character prediction. Since $2k=2\ell-4$, it is the displayed formula. All arguments preserve every $\ell\ge3$ and complete the theorem.

For generic $q$, or whenever the quantum integers needed for $p_r,p_s,p_t$ are units, the unnormalized trivalent theta pairing satisfies

$$\Theta(r,s,t)=\frac{[m]![n']![p]![m+n'+p+1]!}{[m+n']![n'+p]![m+p]!},$$

where $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n'=(s+t-r)/2$, $p=(t+r-s)/2$ are nonnegative integers. The vertices and exact unit domain are those of [[lem-temperley-lieb-general-theta-net-evaluation]]. At $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, the pairing is positive when the triangle/parity conditions hold and $r+s+t\le2\ell-4$; it is zero for a triangle/parity triple above that level. A triple requiring an undefined root JW projector is not implicitly included.

Put $k=\ell-2$ and quotient the diagram category by the tensor ideal generated by $p_{k+1}$. A retained path of length $n$ is $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $a_0=0$, $0\le a_i\le k$ and $|a_i-a_{i-1}|=1$. There are inclusions $i_a:p_{a_n}\to n$ and retractions $r_a:n\to p_{a_n}$ such that $r_ai_b=0$ for distinct paths, $r_ai_a=p_{a_n}$, and $\sum_a i_ar_a=1_n$. Consequently the $E_{a,b}=i_ar_b$ at a common endpoint form complete matrix units, with

$$E_{a,b}E_{c,d}=\delta_{b,c}E_{a,d},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(E_{a,b})=\delta_{a,b}[a_n+1]_q.$$

Their pairing is nondegenerate. The endpoint $p_{k+1}$ is deleted before normalization; no denominator $[\ell]$ is used.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $m=\ell-1$ and $f=p_m$. Put $B_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)$ and

$$J_n=\begin{cases}0,&n<m,\\ B_n(f\otimes1_{n-m})B_n,&n\ge m.\end{cases}$$

If $\mathcal I$ is the categorical tensor ideal generated by $f$, then $\mathcal I(n,n)=J_n$ at every rank. Moreover $\operatorname{ptr}_n(J_n)\subseteq J_{n-1}$. Thus this single embedded two-sided ideal already contains every annular consequence with arbitrary external strands and cups/caps. Below the boundary its component is zero, including contractions given by a partial trace rather than an internal turnback.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

In the pivotal setting of [[def-negligible-morphism-in-a-pivotal-category]], the negligible morphisms are closed under addition, scalar multiplication, arbitrary composition on either side, and tensor product on either side. Thus they form a two-sided tensor ideal. The proof uses an explicit partial-trace identity and does not assume that an arbitrary intertwiner of a tensor product factors as a tensor product of intertwiners.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.

Initially let $q$ be an indeterminate, let $[j]=q^{j-1}+q^{j-3}+\cdots+q^{1-j}$ for $j\ge1$, let $[0]!=1$, and set $\delta=q+q^{-1}$. For nonnegative integers $m,n,p$, put
$$r=m+p,\qquad s=m+n,\qquad t=n+p,\qquad h=m+n+p.$$
Equivalently, $(r,s,t)$ satisfies the triangle inequalities and even-sum condition, with $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n=(s+t-r)/2$, and $p=(t+r-s)/2$. All Jones–Wenzl projectors below have identity coefficient one and are unnormalized.

Let $W_m:0\to2m$ be $m$ nested cups, whose outputs are two consecutive $m$-strand bundles: cup $i$ joins position $i$ of the first bundle to position $m+1-i$ of the second. Let $B_m:2m\to0$ be its horizontal reflection. Define
$$A=1_p\otimes W_m\otimes1_n:t\longrightarrow r+s,\qquad B=1_p\otimes B_m\otimes1_n:r+s\longrightarrow t,$$
$$\alpha=(p_r\otimes p_s)Ap_t,\qquad \beta=p_tB(p_r\otimes p_s),\qquad \Theta(m,n,p)=\operatorname{Tr}_t(\beta\alpha).$$
Thus the pairwise bundles at each trivalent vertex have sizes $m,n,p$: there are $m$ strands between arms $r,s$, $n$ between arms $s,t$, and $p$ between arms $t,r$. This fixes the vertex without a further scalar normalization. The theta net has the three JW-labelled edges $r,s,t$, since idempotence collapses the doubled projectors. Its value is
$$\Theta(m,n,p)=\frac{[m]![n]![p]![h+1]!}{[m+n]![n+p]![m+p]!}.$$
For $p\ge1$ the closed-diagram strip recurrence is
$$[m+p][n+p]\Theta(m,n,p)=[p][m+n+p+1]\Theta(m,n,p-1),\qquad \Theta(m,n,0)=[m+n+1].$$

These identities specialize to every complex $q\ne0$ for which $[j]\ne0$ for $1\le j\le M=\max(r,s,t)$, using the Laurent-polynomial convention at $q=\pm1$. These hypotheses construct the three projectors and make every displayed denominator a unit; $[h+1]$ need not be nonzero. In particular, if $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, then $\Theta>0$ when $h\le\ell-2$, whereas $\Theta=0$ when $h\ge\ell-1$. The latter vertex has zero trace pairing against every reverse morphism. No undefined higher root projector or $0/0$ convention is used.

derivations.claim: Write $m=\ell-1$ and $p=p_m$. It is a nonzero idempotent with one-dimensional corner and trace $[\ell]=0$ by [F3,F4]. For every $x$, cyclic closure gives $\operatorname{Tr}(px)=\operatorname{Tr}(pxp)$; the latter is a scalar multiple of $\operatorname{Tr}(p)=0$. Thus $p$ is negligible. By [F4], the categorical tensor ideal it generates is negligible, and [F2] identifies its endomorphism component as exactly $I_n$. Consequently $I_n\subseteq\operatorname{Rad}(\operatorname{Tr}_n)$ at every rank. The scalar $\delta^{-n}$ exists and does not change this radical.

In the quotient by $I_n$, [F1] gives matrix units $E_{a,b}$ for paths ending at each retained $c$, with trace $\operatorname{Tr}(E_{a,b})=\delta_{a,b}[c+1]$. If an element has a nonzero coefficient at $E_{a,b}$, multiplying by $E_{b,a}$ detects it in this nonzero weighted matrix-trace pairing. The quotient trace pairing is therefore nondegenerate. Together with step 1.1 this proves $I_n=\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)$ and the full matrix-block description. Inserting the path decompositions on both ends describes every unequal-degree Hom space as the corresponding rectangular matrix blocks; its pairing with the reverse Hom space is also nondegenerate. Thus the categorical negligible ideal is precisely the boundary tensor ideal, not a larger ideal known only on endomorphisms. The endpoint corners are $\mathbb Cp_c$, so its additive Karoubi quotient is semisimple with exactly the stated simple labels.

Sandwich a basis matching from $c$ to $a+b$ between $p_c$ and $p_a\otimes p_b$. Any arc joining two points of the same labelled arm is killed by its innermost adjacent turnback. A remaining matching must have the three bundle sizes $(a+b-c)/2$, $(b+c-a)/2$, $(c+a-b)/2$, so it exists only for a triangle/parity triple and is unique. Thus this projected Hom space is spanned by the vertex of [F5], and its reverse by the reflected vertex. Their trace pairing is the exact theta scalar. When the labels are retained, [F5] makes it positive exactly for $a+b+c\le2\ell-4$ and zero above that level. Step 2.1 identifies quotient Hom with this pairing modulo its radical, so its dimension is respectively one or zero. In a semisimple category these are precisely the simple multiplicities in $p_a\otimes p_b$. The triangle, parity and level inequalities yield the displayed truncated rule. No theta value is divided at a forbidden level.

Finally work at rank $m=\ell-1$ **before** quotienting. The same up/down path proof as [F1] applies without deleting its final up endpoint $p_m$: a length-$m$ path cannot exceed height $m$, and every split before its final step uses only $[1],\ldots,[m]$, which are nonzero. All endpoint projectors up to $p_m$ are nonzero by their identity coefficient. The matching-turnback corner calculation gives full matrix units just as before, now including the endpoint $m$; their completeness is the unreduced JW split. Hence $\mathrm{TL}_m$ is semisimple. The endpoint-$m$ block has the unique all-up path and is $\mathbb Cp_m$. Its trace weight is $[m+1]=0$, whereas every other endpoint weight is positive. Thus precisely this one-dimensional block is the trace radical, while semisimplicity makes the Jacobson radical zero. This proves the boundary assertion directly, without assuming a later ordinary semisimplicity criterion.

Fix an integer $\ell\ge3$ and set $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, so the multiplicative order of $q^2$ is $\ell$. Use the divided-power integral form of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] from [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], specialized by $v\mapsto q$ to $\mathbb C$. In type $A_1$, write $K=K_h$ and $E,F$ for the rank-one generators. The convention is

$$KEK^{-1}=q^2E,\qquad KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}F,\qquad [E,F]=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}},$$

$$\Delta(K)=K\otimes K,\qquad \Delta(E)=E\otimes K+1\otimes E,\qquad \Delta(F)=F\otimes1+K^{-1}\otimes F.$$

This is the Sawin coproduct, rather than the inverse-$K$ coproduct in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Its counit is $\varepsilon(K)=1$, $\varepsilon(E)=\varepsilon(F)=0$ and its antipode is $S(E)=-EK^{-1}$, $S(F)=-KF$, $S(K)=K^{-1}$. The exact integral transport is from the library algebra with opposite coproduct, by $E_{\rm target}=KE_{\rm lib}$, $F_{\rm target}=F_{\rm lib}K^{-1}$ and $K_{\rm target}=K_{\rm lib}$. Substituting these generators gives the displayed coproduct and unchanged mixed relation. On divided powers the formulas are $E_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{-r(r-1)}K^rE_{\rm lib}^{(r)}$ and $F_{\rm target}^{(r)}=v^{r(r-1)}F_{\rm lib}^{(r)}K^{-r}$; the inverse formulas also have Laurent-monomial coefficients, so the integral lattice and toral generators are preserved.

The Lusztig specialization includes all divided powers $E^{(r)},F^{(r)}$ and the toral quantum binomials; this is the divided-power form, not the small quantum group. A finite-dimensional module is **type 1** when it carries its integral-weight grading $M=\bigoplus_{m\in\mathbb Z}M_m$ with $K|_{M_m}=q^m$, the full toral character $T_{c,t}|_{M_m}=\begin{bmatrix}m+c\\t\end{bmatrix}_q I$ for every $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$, and $E^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m+2r}$, $F^{(r)}M_m\subseteq M_{m-2r}$. The binomial is its Laurent-polynomial specialization, including negative upper indices. The grading is part of the data and is not collapsed when distinct weights have the same $K$ eigenvalue. Every module intertwiner preserves it: for $m<n$, $T_{-m,n-m}$ has eigenvalues $0$ and $1$ on weights $m$ and $n$.

For $a\ge0$, the Weyl module $\Delta(a)$ has basis $v_0,\ldots,v_a$ and actions

$$Kv_j=q^{a-2j}v_j,\qquad E^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}a-j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j-r},\qquad F^{(r)}v_j=\begin{bmatrix}j+r\\r\end{bmatrix}_qv_{j+r},$$

where the Gaussian binomials are the Laurent-polynomial specializations of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]], and $v_j=0$ outside $0\le j\le a$. Its dual is the dual Weyl module $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. A **Weyl filtration** (respectively dual-Weyl filtration) is a finite submodule filtration whose successive quotients are modules $\Delta(a)$ (respectively $\nabla(a)$). A **tilting module** is a module with both filtrations.

Take $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, so $s^2=q$. The ribbon category is the full weight-lattice extension $\mathcal U_s^\dagger(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ of this Lusztig form, not its root-lattice restriction. Its toral factor is the completed function algebra on the weight lattice $P=\mathbb Z\omega$, acting on each weight space by its weight character. Before specialization, the rank-one universal $R$-matrix is the Sawin weight-lattice expression

$R=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E^{(r)}\otimes F^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$

interpreted in the completed tensor product; at the root it means the image of the integral completed form, not termwise division by a vanishing $[r]_q!$. In ordinary powers the coefficient is $q^{r(r-1)/2}(q-q^{-1})^r/[r]_q!$; changing to two divided powers multiplies that coefficient by $([r]_q!)^2$. Thus the displayed divided-power coefficient is Laurent integral and vanishes for $r\ge\ell$ after specialization. The toral factor is the weight pairing, fixed explicitly by $D$ above. The pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and the twist is $\theta=u^{-1}j$ for the Drinfeld map $u$. The object class of this page is the full subcategory of finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting modules for this weight-lattice ribbon extension. No assertion about semisimplicity or the trace radical is part of this definition.

For every $\ell\ge3$, the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]] is rigid and braided by $c_{M,N}=\operatorname{flip}\circ R_{M,N}$, where

$$R_{M,N}=D\sum_{r\ge0}q^{r(r+1)/2}(1-q^{-2})^r[r]_q!E_M^{(r)}\otimes F_N^{(r)},\qquad D|_{M_m\otimes N_n}=s^{mn}.$$

The sum is finite on every pair of objects. Its pivotal map is $j_M(x)(\varphi)=\varphi(Kx)$ and its ribbon twist is $\theta_M=u_M^{-1}j_M$, with $u$ the Drinfeld map. For $V=\Delta(1)$, the self-dual cup and cap are

$$w=v_+\otimes v_- -q^{-1}v_-\otimes v_+,\qquad b(v_+\otimes v_-)=-q,\quad b(v_-\otimes v_+)=1,$$

with $b(v_\pm\otimes v_\pm)=0$. They obey both snakes, $b(w)=-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$ for $j$. Nevertheless $\dim_j V=\delta$. If $U=-wb$, then $U^2=\delta U$, the adjacent TL relations hold, and

$$c_{V,V}=sI-s^{-1}U,\qquad T=qU-I=-s\,c_{V,V}^{-1}.$$

The $\Delta(2)$ and trivial channels have crossing eigenvalues $s,-s^{-3}$ and Hecke eigenvalues $-1,q^2$, respectively. Their twists are $s^8,1$; $\theta_V=s^3I$. The $\Delta(2)$ channel is removed in the negligible quotient when $\ell=3$. More generally $\theta_{\Delta(a)}=s^{a(a+2)}I$ for $0\le a\le\ell-1$. These assertions include even $\ell$ and use no small-quantum-group substitution.

For generic $q$, or whenever the quantum integers needed for $p_r,p_s,p_t$ are units, the unnormalized trivalent theta pairing satisfies

$$\Theta(r,s,t)=\frac{[m]![n']![p]![m+n'+p+1]!}{[m+n']![n'+p]![m+p]!},$$

where $m=(r+s-t)/2$, $n'=(s+t-r)/2$, $p=(t+r-s)/2$ are nonnegative integers. The vertices and exact unit domain are those of [[lem-temperley-lieb-general-theta-net-evaluation]]. At $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and $0\le r,s,t\le\ell-2$, the pairing is positive when the triangle/parity conditions hold and $r+s+t\le2\ell-4$; it is zero for a triangle/parity triple above that level. A triple requiring an undefined root JW projector is not implicitly included.

Put $k=\ell-2$ and quotient the diagram category by the tensor ideal generated by $p_{k+1}$. A retained path of length $n$ is $a=(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ with $a_0=0$, $0\le a_i\le k$ and $|a_i-a_{i-1}|=1$. There are inclusions $i_a:p_{a_n}\to n$ and retractions $r_a:n\to p_{a_n}$ such that $r_ai_b=0$ for distinct paths, $r_ai_a=p_{a_n}$, and $\sum_a i_ar_a=1_n$. Consequently the $E_{a,b}=i_ar_b$ at a common endpoint form complete matrix units, with

$$E_{a,b}E_{c,d}=\delta_{b,c}E_{a,d},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(E_{a,b})=\delta_{a,b}[a_n+1]_q.$$

Their pairing is nondegenerate. The endpoint $p_{k+1}$ is deleted before normalization; no denominator $[\ell]$ is used.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and $\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. Put

$$\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)=\{x\in\mathrm{TL}_n:\tau_n(xy)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathrm{TL}_n\}.$$

Let $I_n$ be the two-sided ideal generated by $p_{\ell-1}\otimes1_{n-\ell+1}$ for $n\ge\ell-1$, and $I_n=0$ below that rank. Then $I_n=\operatorname{Rad}(\tau_n)$, and $\mathrm{TL}_n/I_n$ is the direct sum of full matrix algebras with multiplicities given by length-$n$ paths from $0$ of heights $0,\ldots,\ell-2$. The additive idempotent-complete negligible quotient has simple labels $0,\ldots,\ell-2$, represented by $p_a$, and

$$a\otimes b\cong\bigoplus_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}c.$$

At $n=\ell-1$ the unreduced algebra is semisimple, while its trace radical is the nonzero one-dimensional block generated by $p_{\ell-1}$. Trace radical and Jacobson radical are therefore distinct at this first boundary.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

Use the full integral-weight divided-power category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], with $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$ and every $\ell\ge3$. The displayed strings define $\Delta(a)$, and $\nabla(a)=\Delta(a)^\vee$. For all $a,b\ge0$,

$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=\delta_{ab},\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^1(\Delta(a),\nabla(b))=0.$$

Here Ext vanishing means that every short exact sequence in the finite-dimensional full-weight category with those end terms splits. The tensor product $\Delta(a)\otimes\Delta(b)$ has one Weyl factor of each label $a+b,a+b-2,\ldots,|a-b|$, and the analogous dual-Weyl assertion holds. Both filtration classes are closed under direct summands. Thus tiltings are closed under tensor products, duals and direct summands. For every $a\ge0$ there is exactly one indecomposable tilting $T(a)$ of highest weight $a$; its weight-$a$ space is one-dimensional, and it occurs as a summand of $V^{\otimes a}$, where $V=\Delta(1)$. Every finite tilting is a finite direct sum of these $T(a)$, so the additive idempotent-complete tensor category generated by $V$ is the entire tilting category.

Let $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $\ell\ge3$, and use the full-weight category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Write $T(m)$ for the indecomposable tilting of highest weight $m$ and $\chi(m)=\sum_{j=0}^m e^{m-2j}$. For $a\ge1$ and $0\le b\le\ell-2$,

$$\operatorname{ch}T(a\ell+b)=\chi(a\ell+b)+\chi(a\ell-b-2),\qquad \operatorname{ch}T(a\ell-1)=\chi(a\ell-1).$$

Also $T(m)=\Delta(m)=\nabla(m)$ for $0\le m<\ell$. With the positive $K$ pivotal map, the dimension on a Weyl character is $[m+1]_q$. Consequently every $T(m)$ with $m\ge\ell-1$ has zero pivotal trace on **every** endomorphism, so its identity is negligible. In the retained range $0\le m\le\ell-2$, $T(m)$ is simple of nonzero pivotal dimension $[m+1]_q$.

For every $\ell\ge3$, let $\mathcal T_\ell$ be the full finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], and $\mathcal N_\ell$ its negligible ideal. The quotient with the same objects and morphism spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(X,Y)/\mathcal N_\ell(X,Y)$ is a finite semisimple ribbon category. Its simple objects are exactly $T(0),\ldots,T(\ell-2)$, of pivotal dimensions $[a+1]_q$, and

$$[T(a)][T(b)]=\sum_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}[T(c)]\qquad(0\le a,b\le\ell-2).$$

Here a fusion category means a $\mathbb C$-linear rigid semisimple monoidal category with simple unit and finitely many simple isomorphism classes. The quotient is spherical with the specified positive pivotal dimensions and inherits the full ribbon structure, including even $\ell$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category with chosen left duals and twist
$\theta$ ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]), let $X\in\mathcal C$, let
$n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, and let $\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the
blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$: the closed framed tangle diagram obtained
from the $(n,n)$-tangle diagram of $\beta$ by joining its top boundary points
to its bottom boundary points by the identity pairing in the blackboard
framing, with every band colored by $X$. Denote by
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ the value of the tangle evaluation functor
on a word in the elementary generators representing this closed diagram. Then

$$t_n(\beta)=F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

where $t_n$ is the ribbon trace of
[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]] and $F_X$ is the tangle
evaluation functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]].
Consequently $t_n(\beta)$ depends only on the framed isotopy class of
$\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$, and the blackboard-framed closure of the positive
stabilization $\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$ is the framed closure of $\beta$ with
one positive curl added on a band, while the closure of the negative
stabilization adds one negative curl; with Turaev's convention the positive
curl is the generator $\varphi_X$ with $F_X(\varphi_X)=\theta_X$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural
isomorphism $u$ with the natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity. It is
**monoidal** up to the monoidal comparison $d_{X,Y}\colon
X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual
functor,

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation
$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for
the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

Let $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), and let
$\rho_n\colon B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(X^{\otimes n})$ be the
canonical braid action
([[cor-an-object-of-a-braided-category-carries-canonical-braid-actions]]). The
**ribbon evaluation** of the $X$-colored closed braid is the value

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

in the sense of
[[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]: the composite
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)$ is a morphism
$X^{\otimes n}\to(X^{\otimes n})^{\vee\vee}$, which is exactly the input type of
the left categorical trace. When $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$
the value $t_n(\beta)$ is a scalar. For $n=1$ the group $B_1$ is trivial and
$t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X)$, the left dimension of $X$.

For $n=0$ put $t_0(e)=1_{\mathbf 1}$, the evaluation of the empty
closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing
is needed for the empty diagram.

The identification of $t_n(\beta)$ with the evaluation
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ of the blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$
under the functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is
the content of the closure-comparison lemma of this page; it must be proved
before the trace is used as a link evaluation, and it is not assumed here. The
functor $F_X$ is constructed under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), while the definition of $t_n$ above is choice-free
and uses neither that functor nor that principle; only the comparison, not the
trace, carries the choice cost.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

These are the right coevaluation and evaluation on $X$ induced by the ribbon
structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the genuine full-algebra intertwiners $w,b$ satisfy both snakes, $b(w)=-\delta$ and $KB^t=-B$ for their bilinear form. Thus the self-duality sign is $-1$, independently of rescaling. Put $e=wb$ and $U=-e=\delta P_0$. The snakes give $U_i^2=\delta U_i$, $U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i$ and distant commutation, so they give every $\rho_n$. The two channels and their twists/crossings are exactly [F1]. In particular $T=qU-1=-s c^{-1}$, so $q^2$ belongs to the trivial channel, not to the highest-weight-$2$ channel.

The rigid tensor functor from $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$ sends cup to $w$, cap to $b$, and $e_i$ to $w_ib_i$. The two snakes and negative loop verify its defining matching relations. The algebra identification $U_i\mapsto-e_i$ preserves the JW projectors: the recursion quantum integers for loop $-\delta$ are $(-1)^{j-1}[j]$, and these signs cancel against the generator sign in each recursive correction. Thus the evaluated projector $p_a$ is annihilated by the matrices $U_i$. For $a\le\ell-1$, their common kernel in each weight space is one-dimensional: $U_i$ imposes that the coefficient of $-+$ is $q$ times that of $+-$, so adjacent swaps determine every coefficient from one word. The vectors $F^{(j)}v_+^{\otimes a}$, $0\le j\le a$, belong to this kernel and are nonzero: the divided coproduct has one Laurent-monomial coefficient for every specified subset of $j$ changed positions. The projector acts as identity on its common kernel, since its nonidentity generator words kill that kernel. Its image is therefore precisely this $(a+1)$-dimensional highest-weight string, equal to $\Delta(a)$ by [F4]. In particular $p_{\ell-1}$ has a nonzero image of zero pivotal dimension, and cannot lie in the kernel of the unreduced map.

In the quantum negligible quotient the boundary image is zero by [F4]. Transport [F2]'s path splits to the negative-loop category. Its down normalization is $-\lambda_a$ rather than $\lambda_a=[a+1]/[a]$; replacing its down cap map by its negative yields exactly the positive-algebra normalization for $U=-e$. The transported path units therefore have the same multiplication and positive-$K$ trace weights $[a+1]$. They decompose $V^{\otimes n}$ into all retained $\Delta(a)$ copies. Hom orthogonality in [F4] shows their rectangular blocks are the **entire** quantum quotient Hom spaces, not a proper subalgebra. Their positive trace weights show independence, while [F2] identifies the diagram kernel as exactly $I_n$. This proves the displayed centralizer isomorphism. On a chosen retained sum $R_n$, composites through discarded negligible summands are zero because its weighted matrix-trace pairing is nondegenerate. Thus projecting to $R_n$ realizes the same algebra as $\operatorname{End}_U(R_n)$; the quotient formulation is independent of that choice.

The same path decomposition on both ends gives fullness and faithfulness for Hom spaces between unequal tensor degrees as well. Every tilting is a sum of summands of powers of $V$ by [F4]. Consequently the functor extends from the additive Karoubi boundary quotient of $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$ to a tensor equivalence with the whole tilting negligible quotient. In the source let $j_0$ be its planar pivotal structure. Its dimension at $p_a$ is $(-1)^a[a+1]$. The parity map $\epsilon_n=(-1)^n1_n$ is a monoidal natural automorphism: Hom spaces between different parities are zero. It descends to summands with $\epsilon_{p_a}=(-1)^a$ and commutes with duality. Thus $j=\epsilon j_0$ has the positive dimensions $[a+1]$. More precisely, the equality $KB^t=-B$ in step 1.1 says the functor's transported planar pivotal map on $V$ is $-K$; multiplying it by $\epsilon_V=-1$ gives exactly $K$. Monoidality, direct sums and summands prove equality of pivotal structures on every object, not merely equality of dimensions.

The source crossing $c=s1+s^{-1}e$ is precisely the actual finite-$R$ crossing by [F1]. Its inverse and adjacent triple relations hold by the TL relations. Naturality with cups/caps can also be read directly: for $W_1=w\otimes1$, $W_2=1\otimes w$, the snakes give $e_1W_1=-\delta W_1$, $e_2W_1=W_2$, $e_1W_2=W_1$, so $c_1c_2W_1=(s^2-\delta+s^{-2})W_1+W_2=W_2$; the reflected and reversed identities give the other three slides. Thus the functor preserves the full braiding. With $j_0$, the generator curl is $s(-s^2-s^{-2})+s^{-1}=-s^3$. Since $\theta=u^{-1}j$, changing $j_0$ to $\epsilon j_0$ changes this to $+s^3$. Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, let $\delta\in R$, and let $n\ge0$. Let $t$ be an integer with $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even. The diagram module $M_R(n,t)$ has $n$ bottom boundary points and $t$ top boundary points, with stacking and loop removal as in [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. A component of a basis diagram is **propagating** if it meets both the bottom and top boundaries. Write $\operatorname{prop}(D)$ for the number of propagating components of a diagram $D:n\to t$.

Let $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ be the $R$-span of the basis diagrams $D:n\to t$ with $\operatorname{prop}(D)<t$. Define the **Temperley–Lieb link-state standard module**

$$W_{n,t}(R,\delta):=M_R(n,t)/M_R^{<t}(n,t).$$

Write $T_{n,t}$ for the set of diagrams in $\mathcal D(n,t)$ with exactly $t$ propagating components. The cosets of these diagrams form an $R$-basis of $W_{n,t}$. Identifying each diagram with its bottom arcs and defects gives a partial matching of the $n$ ordered bottom sites, with the additional condition that the $t$ unpaired sites are joined to the ordered top sites by noncrossing propagating strands. In particular, no defect lies inside an arc. The unpaired sites are called **defects**. Thus $t$ is the defect or through-line number; in sources using $p$ for the number of arcs, $p=(n-t)/2$.

The intended right action of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$, where $x\in M_R(n,t)$, $a\in M_R(n,n)$, and $x\circ a$ stacks $x$ above $a$. The submodule $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ is stable under this action, so it descends to $W_{n,t}$; the complete well-definedness argument is [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-module-action-is-well-defined]].

For $R$, $\delta$, $n$, $t$ and $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ as in [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]], the rule $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$ defines a unital right $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$-module structure on $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

For every commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and objects $m,n,p,q\ge0$, the raw diagram data of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]] form a strict monoidal category $\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)$ with hom-modules $M_R(m,n)$ and the stated $R$-bilinear stacking composition. Composition is associative, the identity diagrams are two-sided identities, and horizontal juxtaposition is a strict monoidal bifunctor with unit object $0$. Consequently $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)}(n)=\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is a unital associative $R$-algebra whose underlying $R$-module is free on its noncrossing pairing diagrams.

Let $R$, $\delta$, $n$, $t$ and $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ be as in [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]]. For link states $x,y$, let $x^*$ denote reflection across a horizontal line. The diagram $y\circ x^*:t\to t$ is either $\delta^c1_t$ for some $c\ge0$ or has fewer than $t$ propagating components. Define $\phi_{n,t}(x,y)=\delta^c$ in the first case and $0$ in the second, and extend $R$-bilinearly. Then $\phi_{n,t}$ is symmetric and satisfies

$$\phi_{n,t}(x\cdot a,y)=\phi_{n,t}(x,y\cdot a^*)$$

for all $x,y\in W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ and $a\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. Here $a^*$ is reflection across a horizontal line. The matrix of $\phi_{n,t}$ in the link-state basis is the Gram matrix obtained by reflecting and capping two link states, with one factor $\delta$ for each closed loop.

Let $F$ be a field, $\delta\in F$, and $n\ge0$. Put $D_{n,t}=W_{n,t}(F,\delta)/\operatorname{rad}(\phi_{n,t})$ for each allowed $t$. Then the nonzero $D_{n,t}$ are absolutely simple and form a complete set of pairwise nonisomorphic simple right $\mathrm{TL}_n(F,\delta)$-modules. Moreover, $D_{n,t}\ne0$ exactly when $\phi_{n,t}$ is not identically zero; in that case $\operatorname{rad}(\phi_{n,t})$ is the unique maximal proper submodule and $D_{n,t}$ is the simple head of $W_{n,t}$. If $\phi_{n,t}$ is identically zero, then $D_{n,t}=0$, but no conclusion about the actual head of $W_{n,t}$ follows.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, let $\delta\in R$, and let $n\ge0$. Let $t$ be an integer with $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even. The diagram module $M_R(n,t)$ has $n$ bottom boundary points and $t$ top boundary points, with stacking and loop removal as in [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. A component of a basis diagram is **propagating** if it meets both the bottom and top boundaries. Write $\operatorname{prop}(D)$ for the number of propagating components of a diagram $D:n\to t$.

Let $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ be the $R$-span of the basis diagrams $D:n\to t$ with $\operatorname{prop}(D)<t$. Define the **Temperley–Lieb link-state standard module**

$$W_{n,t}(R,\delta):=M_R(n,t)/M_R^{<t}(n,t).$$

Write $T_{n,t}$ for the set of diagrams in $\mathcal D(n,t)$ with exactly $t$ propagating components. The cosets of these diagrams form an $R$-basis of $W_{n,t}$. Identifying each diagram with its bottom arcs and defects gives a partial matching of the $n$ ordered bottom sites, with the additional condition that the $t$ unpaired sites are joined to the ordered top sites by noncrossing propagating strands. In particular, no defect lies inside an arc. The unpaired sites are called **defects**. Thus $t$ is the defect or through-line number; in sources using $p$ for the number of arcs, $p=(n-t)/2$.

The intended right action of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$, where $x\in M_R(n,t)$, $a\in M_R(n,n)$, and $x\circ a$ stacks $x$ above $a$. The submodule $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ is stable under this action, so it descends to $W_{n,t}$; the complete well-definedness argument is [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-module-action-is-well-defined]].

For $R$, $\delta$, $n$, $t$ and $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ as in [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]], the rule $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$ defines a unital right $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$-module structure on $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$.

For $0\le k\le n$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the polynomial $\sum_w Q^{\operatorname{inv}(w)}$, summed over binary words with $k$ ones and $n-k$ zeros, where $\operatorname{inv}(w)$ counts pairs with a one to the left of a zero. There is a unique polynomial $B_{n,k}(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]$ such that

$$B_{n,k}(q+q^{-1})=q^{-k(n-k)}G_{n,k}(q^2).$$

It agrees as a rational-function identity with $[n]!/([k]![n-k]!)$; its value at a specialized loop parameter is the polynomial value, without division by vanishing factorials.

For a field $K$, $\delta\in K$, recurrence quantum characteristic $\ell$, and $p=\operatorname{char}K$, every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ for $0\le k\le n$ is nonzero exactly as follows: if $\ell=\infty$, at every finite $n$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p>0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell p^{i-1}-1$ with $i\ge1$ and $1\le a<p$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p=0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell-1$ for a positive integer $a$.

Use the digits and place values in [[def-temperley-lieb-spencer-digit-support]], and write $N+1=\sum_{j=0}^r n_js_j$ with $n_r>0$. When $\ell<\infty$, each signed expression $\sum_j\varepsilon_jn_js_j-1$ with $\varepsilon_r=1$ lies in $[0,N]$, has parity $N$, and determines its signs at every nonzero digit uniquely. Thus the support has $2^h$ elements, where $h$ is the number of nonzero digits below $r$.

For $0\le v\le u$, the specialized quantum binomial $B_{u,v}(\delta)$ is nonzero exactly when each mixed-radix digit of $v$ is at most the corresponding digit of $u$. In characteristic zero this uses the two digits with places $1,\ell$; if $\ell=\infty$, every such binomial is nonzero.

For any $0<k\le r$, changing all signs at indices less than $k$ reflects the corresponding support element about the wall $H-1$, where $H=\sum_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ is a positive multiple of $s_k$. In particular, writing $L=\sum_{j<k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ gives the pair $H+L-1,H-L-1$ and $|L|<s_k$.

Let $a,b,c$ belong to this support, and suppose their sets of negative nonzero digits satisfy $A\subseteq B\subseteq C$. Then $a\ge b\ge c$ and the specialized quantum binomial
$$B_{(a-c)/2,(a-b)/2}(\delta)$$
is nonzero. Here $B$ denotes the polynomial quantum binomial of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]]. If $\ell=\infty$, the same last assertion holds for the only triple $a=b=c=N$.

Let $K$ be a field, let $\delta\in K$, and let $\ell$ be the recurrence quantum characteristic of $(K,\delta)$ from [[def-temperley-lieb-quantum-integers-and-quantum-characteristic]]. Put $P=\operatorname{char}K$ when $\operatorname{char}K>0$, and put $P=\infty$ when $\operatorname{char}K=0$. In this definition $\ell$ is Spencer's recurrence parameter; it is not the complex order $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$.

Suppose first that $\ell<\infty$. Set $s_0=1$ and $s_i=\ell P^{i-1}$ for each $i\ge1$ with $P<\infty$. If $P=\infty$, set $s_1=\ell$ and omit all $s_i$ for $i\ge2$. Every $M\in\mathbb N$ has a unique expansion
$$M=\sum_{i=0}^{r}m_i s_i,$$
where $0\le m_0<\ell$ and $0\le m_i<P$ for $i\ge1$ when $P<\infty$. When $P=\infty$, write $M=m_0+m_1\ell$ with $0\le m_0<\ell$ and $m_1\ge0$; if $m_1=0$, take $r=0$. The highest digit $m_r$ is nonzero unless $M=0$, for which take $r=0$ and $m_0=0$.

For a label $N\ge0$, let $n_i$ be the digits of $N+1$, so $N+1=\sum_{i=0}^{r}n_i s_i$. Define the **Spencer support set**
$$\operatorname{Supp}_{\ell,P}(N)= \left\{\sum_{i=0}^{r}\varepsilon_i n_i s_i-1: \varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\},\ \varepsilon_r=1,\ \sum_{i=0}^{r}\varepsilon_i n_i s_i-1\ge0\right\}.$$
If $\ell=\infty$, define $\operatorname{Supp}_{\ell,P}(N)=\{N\}$.

This item defines the digit expansion and a finite set only. Spencer's theorem identifying these sets with decomposition multiplicities, and the separate Jones–Wenzl existence criterion, are not asserted here; both require the full field hypotheses and their own proofs.

Let $K$ be any field, $\delta\in K$, and let $0\le r\le n$ with $n-r$ even. Assume $r>0$ or $\delta\ne0$ or $n=r=0$. Put $A_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$, use the right modules $W_{n,t}$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]], and put $D_{n,t}=W_{n,t}/\operatorname{rad}\phi_{n,t}$. There are $y,z:n\to r$ with $y\circ z^*=1_r$, and for $r>0$ both may be chosen as basis monic diagrams. There is an idempotent $e\in A_n$ with $eA_ne\cong A_r$ such that $M\mapsto Me$ is exact, sends $W_{n,t}$ to $W_{r,t}$, and sends $D_{n,t}$ to $D_{r,t}$, with value zero when $t>r$.

Consequently, for every allowed $m$,
$$[W_{n,m}:D_{n,r}]=[W_{r,m}:D_{r,r}],$$
where $W_{r,m}=0$ if $m>r$. The module $D_{r,r}=W_{r,r}$ is one dimensional and every diagram generator acts by zero. Thus the decomposition problem reduces exactly to multiplicities of this trivial module. The excluded case $n>r=0,\delta=0$ has $D_{n,0}=0$ and is not a simple label.

derivations.claim: We first use loop value $-T$. Consider matchings with a fixed finite number $d$ of cups on a half-infinite ordered row, with all sufficiently far-left sites propagating. A diagram is encoded by the $d$ right cup endpoints, numbered from the right starting at $1$: scanning from right to left, a listed site opens a cup and the next unpaired unlisted site closes the most recent cup; unlisted sites with no open cup propagate. Thus every $d$-element subset of the positive integers encodes exactly one matching. Hook weights are unchanged by adding more leftmost propagating strands, because bending one more such strand adds a root above the entire old forest and cancels its new numerator factor. We may consequently form the formal series $V_d$ of these matchings with their hook weights. Every fixed output coefficient after a local generator or cup attachment involves finitely many terms: only its finitely many cups and the nearest exposed propagating strand can be reconnected. All operations below are defined coefficient by coefficient.

We prove that every local generator kills $V_d$. Fix an output matching $D$ with its simple cup at sites $i,i+1$, and remove that cup to obtain a gap $J$ in $D^-$. A line is exposed to $J$ if an arc from $J$ to an interior point of that line can avoid all other lines. Replacing that line by two lines ending at $i$ and $i+1$ is its nip at $J$. Exactly $D$ itself and these nipped diagrams are the preimages contributing to the coefficient of $D$: a generator changes only the two lines meeting its sites, while the converse reconnection recovers each nip. A line exposed on both sides is nipped only once. Therefore the coefficient is $C_D=-[2]_T h(D)+\sum_{e\text{ exposed to }J}h(\operatorname{nip}_J(e)).$ This enumeration includes loops through the first term and all reconnection terms with coefficient $1$.

Here is a textual reduction verifying this coefficient identity. First contract each intervening fixed internal subforest to a weighted interval block: its total edge count is retained in the containing arc's subtree size and its own hook factors are common to all compared terms. Consecutive exposed arcs then have adjacent block endpoints; relabel these endpoints in their order without changing subtree sizes. Suppose those two arcs have endpoints $(a,b),(b+1,c)$, with all their internal subforests retained, and the distinguished simple cup is immediately beyond them at $(c+1,c+2)$. Replace those two arcs by $(a,c),(b,b+1)$. If their subtree sizes are $E_1,E_2$, their merged subtree has size $E_1+E_2$. Every term in $C_D$ other than the two nips of these arcs corresponds to the replaced diagram with hook ratio $[E_1+E_2]_T/([E_1]_T[E_2]_T)$. Comparing the two exceptional nips with the single exceptional nip after replacement leaves a common rational factor times $[E_2]_T[E_1+E_2+1]_T+[E_1]_T-[E_2+1]_T[E_1+E_2]_T=0.$ To verify the ratios, every unchanged arc contributes the same denominator factor; the changed arcs contribute respectively the subtree sizes $E_1,E_2,E_1+E_2,E_2+1,E_1+E_2+1$. The displayed identity follows by induction on $E_1$ from the recurrence for $[j]_T$, with $E_1=0,1$ as immediate base cases. Thus this replacement preserves the vanishing of $C_D$. The reflected replacement does the same on the other side. Each replacement reduces by one the number of exposed arcs on the chosen side; repeated replacements leave at most one exposed arc on each side.

In the half-infinite setting there is always a leftmost propagating strand beyond all the cups under consideration. Bend that strand and the other output strands to put the distinguished cup and the remaining exposed arcs inside one outer arc. This only adds successive roots as in step 2.1. After the reductions of step 4.1, let the sizes of the optional left and right exposed subtrees be $B,C>0$. Canceling the hook factors of unchanged internal subforests, the four contributions in step 3.1 have the common-factor-normalized sum $-\frac{[2]_T}{[B]_T[C]_T[B+C+2]_T}+\frac1{[B+1]_T[C+1]_T[B]_T[C]_T}+\frac1{[B+1]_T[C]_T[B+C+2]_T}+\frac1{[B]_T[C+1]_T[B+C+2]_T}=0.$ The numerator is $-[2]_T[B+1]_T[C+1]_T+[B+C+2]_T+[B]_T[C+1]_T+[C]_T[B+1]_T$, zero by the same recurrence. If the left subtree is absent, the three terms reduce instead to $-[2]_T/([C]_T[C+2]_T)+1/([C+1]_T[C]_T)+1/([C+1]_T[C+2]_T)$, zero because $[C+2]_T+[C]_T=[2]_T[C+1]_T$. The case of no right subtree is its reflection. If neither is present, the sum is $-[2]_T/[2]_T+1=0$. Thus $C_D=0$ in every case, proving the assertion of step 3.1 as a polynomial identity.

A formal vector killed by every generator is uniquely determined by its coefficient on the fully nested rightmost $d$ cups. Indeed order the endpoint subsets componentwise, with minimum $\{1,\ldots,d\}$. For any other subset $J$, let $i>1$ be its least element with $i-1\notin J$, and replace $i$ by $i-1$ to obtain $K<J$. In the coefficient at $K$ after applying the generator at $i-1,i$, the coefficient at $J$ occurs with coefficient $1$. Every other contributing subset $L$ satisfies $L<J$: nipping a line different from the one producing $J$ moves an endpoint closer to the right boundary, and the loop term is $K<J$. Setting this coefficient to zero therefore determines the coefficient at $J$ from smaller subsets. Componentwise lower sets are finite, so induction applies. This proof is valid over $\mathbb Z[T]$ and after any specialization.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$. Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of $t$ with $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even, ordered by $\lambda_r\unrhd\lambda_t$ exactly when $r\le t$. Thus labels with fewer propagating strands are strictly greater. For $x,y\in T_{n,t}$, define

$$C^t_{x,y}:=x^*\circ y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,δ),$$

where $x,y:n\to t$ are link-state diagrams and $*$ is reflection across a horizontal line. Then the diagrams $C^t_{x,y}$, for all $t\in\Lambda_n$ and $x,y\in T_{n,t}$, form an $R$-basis of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, and $(C,\Lambda_n)$ is a cellular basis in the convention of [[def-cellular-algebra-basis-and-cell-module]]. Its cell module at $\lambda_t$ is $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$, and its cell form is the Gram form $\phi_{n,t}$ of [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-gram-form-is-invariant]].

Let $F$ be a field, $\delta\in F$, and $n\ge0$. Put $D_{n,t}=W_{n,t}(F,\delta)/\operatorname{rad}(\phi_{n,t})$ for each allowed $t$. Then the nonzero $D_{n,t}$ are absolutely simple and form a complete set of pairwise nonisomorphic simple right $\mathrm{TL}_n(F,\delta)$-modules. Moreover, $D_{n,t}\ne0$ exactly when $\phi_{n,t}$ is not identically zero; in that case $\operatorname{rad}(\phi_{n,t})$ is the unique maximal proper submodule and $D_{n,t}$ is the simple head of $W_{n,t}$. If $\phi_{n,t}$ is identically zero, then $D_{n,t}=0$, but no conclusion about the actual head of $W_{n,t}$ follows.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, $n\ge1$, and let $t$ be allowed for $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$. Include $\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}(R,\delta)$ into $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ by adding a rightmost vertical strand, and restrict the right action along this inclusion. Set $W_{m,s}=0$ when $s<0$, $s>m$, or $m-s$ is odd. Then there is a short exact sequence of right $\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}(R,\delta)$-modules

$$0\longrightarrow W_{n-1,t-1}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Res}^{TL_n}_{TL_{n-1}}W_{n,t}\longrightarrow W_{n-1,t+1}\longrightarrow0.$$

The sequence gives a two-step filtration; it is not asserted to split.

Let $K$ be any field, $\delta\in K$, and let $0\le r\le n$ with $n-r$ even. Assume $r>0$ or $\delta\ne0$ or $n=r=0$. Put $A_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$, use the right modules $W_{n,t}$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]], and put $D_{n,t}=W_{n,t}/\operatorname{rad}\phi_{n,t}$. There are $y,z:n\to r$ with $y\circ z^*=1_r$, and for $r>0$ both may be chosen as basis monic diagrams. There is an idempotent $e\in A_n$ with $eA_ne\cong A_r$ such that $M\mapsto Me$ is exact, sends $W_{n,t}$ to $W_{r,t}$, and sends $D_{n,t}$ to $D_{r,t}$, with value zero when $t>r$.

Consequently, for every allowed $m$,
$$[W_{n,m}:D_{n,r}]=[W_{r,m}:D_{r,r}],$$
where $W_{r,m}=0$ if $m>r$. The module $D_{r,r}=W_{r,r}$ is one dimensional and every diagram generator acts by zero. Thus the decomposition problem reduces exactly to multiplicities of this trivial module. The excluded case $n>r=0,\delta=0$ has $D_{n,0}=0$ and is not a simple label.

Use the digits and place values in [[def-temperley-lieb-spencer-digit-support]], and write $N+1=\sum_{j=0}^r n_js_j$ with $n_r>0$. When $\ell<\infty$, each signed expression $\sum_j\varepsilon_jn_js_j-1$ with $\varepsilon_r=1$ lies in $[0,N]$, has parity $N$, and determines its signs at every nonzero digit uniquely. Thus the support has $2^h$ elements, where $h$ is the number of nonzero digits below $r$.

For $0\le v\le u$, the specialized quantum binomial $B_{u,v}(\delta)$ is nonzero exactly when each mixed-radix digit of $v$ is at most the corresponding digit of $u$. In characteristic zero this uses the two digits with places $1,\ell$; if $\ell=\infty$, every such binomial is nonzero.

For any $0<k\le r$, changing all signs at indices less than $k$ reflects the corresponding support element about the wall $H-1$, where $H=\sum_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ is a positive multiple of $s_k$. In particular, writing $L=\sum_{j<k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ gives the pair $H+L-1,H-L-1$ and $|L|<s_k$.

Let $a,b,c$ belong to this support, and suppose their sets of negative nonzero digits satisfy $A\subseteq B\subseteq C$. Then $a\ge b\ge c$ and the specialized quantum binomial
$$B_{(a-c)/2,(a-b)/2}(\delta)$$
is nonzero. Here $B$ denotes the polynomial quantum binomial of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]]. If $\ell=\infty$, the same last assertion holds for the only triple $a=b=c=N$.

Write $[j]_T$ for the polynomial recurrence $[0]_T=0,[1]_T=1,[j+1]_T=T[j]_T-[j-1]_T$. For a monic diagram $x:a\to b$, bend its $b$ output points around the right edge in reverse order to form a matching on $a+b$ points. Its nesting forest $F(x)$ consists of its $(a+b)/2$ arcs, ordered by containment. For an arc $e$, let $c(e)$ be the number of arcs inside it, counting itself. Define the polynomial hook weight
$$h_F(T)=\frac{[|F|]_T!}{\prod_{e\in F}[c(e)]_T}.$$
For $a\ge b$ of the same parity, define the nonzero vector
$$v_{a,b}=\sum_{x:a\to b\text{ monic}}h_{F(x)}(-\delta)x\in W_{a,b}.$$
Its coefficient on the diagram whose bent forest is a chain is $1$.

For $a\ge b\ge c$ of the same parity, composition modulo propagation less than $c$ satisfies
$$v_{a,b}\circ v_{b,c}=B_{(a-c)/2,(a-b)/2}(-\delta)v_{a,c}.$$
Composition here means attaching the indicated linear combinations of monic diagrams, in source-to-target order.

Let $s_k$ be an available finite place value of [[def-temperley-lieb-spencer-digit-support]]. If $b<a<b+2s_k$ and $a+b+2$ is divisible by $2s_k$, then postcomposition by $v_{a,b}$ induces a nonzero module homomorphism $W_{n,a}\to W_{n,b}$ for every $n\ge a$ of the same parity.

Let $\chi_j(x)=(x^{j+1}-x^{-j-1})/(x-x^{-1})$ for $j\ge0$, and set $\chi_{-1}=0$. These are integer Laurent polynomials. Put $F_0=0$ and, for $M>0$,
$$F_M(x)=\sum_{m\in\operatorname{Supp}(M-1)}\chi_m(x).$$
For every $n\ge1$, there are nonnegative integers $\beta_{n,r}$, for the labels $0\le r\le n$ of parity $n$, with $\beta_{n,n}=1$, such that
$$ (x+x^{-1})F_n(x)=\sum_{r}\beta_{n,r}F_{r+1}(x).$$
Whenever $r<n$ and $\beta_{n,r}>0$, the actual module $W_{n,r}(K,\delta)$ is simple. If $\delta=0$, $n>0$ is even, and the field is arbitrary, then $\beta_{n,0}=0$. Equivalently, writing $d(r,m)=1$ for $m\in\operatorname{Supp}(r)$ and $0$ otherwise,
$$d(n-1,m-1)+d(n-1,m+1)=\sum_{r\ge m}d(r,m)\beta_{n,r},$$
with out-of-range labels interpreted as zero.
